newsitem.title: Singapore: Asian crude firmer, Oman consolidates discounts.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, Oman consolidates discounts.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer on Wednesday but Oman crude consolidated its position trading at a discount to its official selling price for April. Meanwhile, front-month Dubai crude was firmer reflecting a squeeze in the month, brokers said.
A trader sold a Dubai cargo to a European major at full-month quotes +47 cents and a European major sold a cargo to a U.S. major at full-month quotes +48 cents, traders said.
The deals reflected a much firmer tone for Dubai, which had traded in recent days around +40 and +41 cents. But Dubai was the only crude showing a stronger differential.
Traders reported several Oman deals at discounts to the MPM of one to five cents. The lowest discounted trade was between a Malaysian trader and a Japanese shosha.
Indonesia grades suffered from a dearth of buyers and several trades were talked, although traders were not able to pin point who had done the trades.
Duri was said to have traded as low as ICP -30 cents and Minas as low as ICP -10 cents, but traders remained sceptical so long as information on the deals remained scant.
Traders said the unexpected shut down of 125,000-bpd Balongan refinery would add to the woes of the Indonesian grades.
The refinery was shut down owing to technical problems. The 120,000-bpd Dumai refinery is already shut down for scheduled maintenance.
Traders said Indonesia had a surplus of crude because of the shut downs, but there would be extremely limited appetite among lifters to take on extra allocations.
However, Pertamina might well look to store the crude as it has done in the past.
